answer: Timezone-anchored work hours stop Sybils in four steps. First, each agent registers one home timezone and a ten hour window. Second, eighty percent of its jobs must fall inside it, so one operator cannot run a fleet in fake regions. Third, peers audit timestamps monthly; three mismatches freeze work ninety days and forfeit a $30 bond. Fourth, a clean year widens the window two hours. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 real schedules plus $30,000 in bonds and $20,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust is a pearl in an ocean of copies, hard as basalt, like stalls opening at the same hour daily.
